subject: Recap: Pilot economics & constraints — next steps
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Alex Jones <alex.jones@glacierbank.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 11 Aug 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Recap: Pilot economics & constraints — next steps

Alex — great conversation this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have a single place to align.

Top pain points you shared
- High per-call cost driven by long-context prompts (median 950 tokens, tail to 5k).
- Strict p95 latency requirement: ~<300ms for small inference paths; some less-sensitive batch flows can tolerate up to 1s.
- Compliance: logs & retention policy (7 years), and data residency in us-west for regulated accounts.
- Budget construct: procurement wants to cap pilot spend; rough target ~ $25k–30k/month unless ROI case solidifies.

Goals for pilot
- Validate token-economics and per-conversation unit cost at production traffic (sample traffic will drive estimates).
- Demonstrate 20–30% effective cost reduction via batching + KV prefix caching, with latency kept under your SLO for interactive flows.
- Produce an ops checklist (SLA, fallbacks) to show feasibility for Q1 rollout.

Redwood proposal (high level)
1) Pilot scope (8 weeks): host a 3-month pilot but with an 8-week sizing & tuning window to validate assumptions.
2) Two candidate configurations to model:
   a) Hosted API + aggressive batching & intelligent prefix caching (lower capital outlay, runs on shared hosted infra).
   b) Dedicated pool (reserved GPUs) with quantized LLM variant for tighter p95 latency predictability (higher committed spend, lower unit variance).
3) Cost levers we'll evaluate: token batching frequency, KV/prefix cache hit rate, quantized model delta, and request routing to cheaper compatible variants during burst.

Asks from GlacierBank to produce a realistic cost model
- A 48–72 hour sample: CSV of recent request logs (timestamp, user_id anonymized, prompt token count, response token count, latency) — this lets us produce cost by percentile.
- Your expected average daily concurrent requests and any peak windows.
- Any compliance constraints that would change model choices (e.g., must run in VPC/on-prem).

Budget & timeline framing
- Ballpark pilot cost estimates (before we get your logs): hosted pilot ~$18–28k/month depending on token volume & batching; dedicated pilot ~$28–45k/month but with more predictable p95. These are directional — we will run a micro-sensitivity model after we get sample traffic.
- We recommend starting the sizing window within 2–3 weeks so we can iterate with your SRE and measure cache hit rates.

Next steps (proposed)
- You share sample traffic CSV (see asks) by EOD Tue (Aug 15).
- Redwood will deliver a 2-slide micro-cost model + recommended pilot config by Aug 18.
- Quick follow-up call to align on pilot contract – propose Tue Aug 22, 30m.

Attachments: pilot-scope-draft.pdf (one-page scope + pricing bands)

Thanks again — I’ll loop Rafael and Marissa on the cost modeling.

Best,

Kimberly Park
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.com | (415) 555-0172
Redwood Inference
From: Alex Jones <alex.jones@glacierbank.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 11 Aug 2028 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap: Pilot economics & constraints — next steps

Kimberly — thanks for the write-up, that mirrors our notes. A few quick clarifications and I attached a short sample: glacier-sample-traffic.csv.

- Confirmed: median ~900–1k tokens, 99th percentile ~4.8k depending on user flow.
- Latency SLO: interactive product surfaces need p95 <= 300ms; background batch processing can be up to 1s.
- Compliance: logs must stay in us-west and be retained 7 years. No on-prem requirement for the pilot but production may require a VPC option.

Budget: procurement gave a hard ceiling of $25k for the initial pilot window but said there is flexibility if we can show a path to net positive ROI in Q4.

I’ve attached the sample traffic CSV (anonymized) and a short note from our SRE about peak windows. We can target Aug 22 for the follow-up — Tue morning preferred.

-Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Alex Jones
Head of AI Platforms, GlacierBank
alex.jones@glacierbank.com | (206) 555-1414

Attachment: glacier-sample-traffic.csv
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 11 Aug 2028 13:20:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Recap: Pilot economics & constraints — next steps

Rafael / Marissa — forwarding Alex’s reply + sample CSV. Action items: please review and come back with a draft micro-cost model and recommended pilot config by EOD Mon. I want two flavors:

1) Low-commit hosted pilot that prioritizes cost-efficiency (include expected batching hit rates & resulting per-conversation cost).
2) Predictable-latency dedicated variant with estimated committed spend and expected p95 improvements.

Specific asks for the model: use the sample CSV (attached) and show sensitivity to cache hit rate (0%, 25%, 50%), batching latency tradeoffs, and quantized model performance assumptions. Highlight the minimum expected unit cost to meet the 300ms p95.

I’ll prep the Aug 22 call invite for Tue 10:00am PT unless you flag a time conflict. Rafael, can you own the dedicated-config numbers? Marissa — please lead the hosted/batching analysis.

Thanks — K

--
Kimberly Park
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
